game: SF @ SEA, Week 5 2026, morning of kickoff (spread/total/weather/kick time not saved; outdoor Lumen assumed)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is inferred from weeks 2-4 only. Both run defenses have been stingy (SEA 3.73 YPC and 5 passes of 20+; SF 3.77 YPC and only 3 runs of 10+), so the points path is the pass game, not a ground gash. Base case is a competitive, pass-leaning game: SEA's offense is JSN (31 targets, 359 yards, 338 air over weeks 2-4) with Emanuel Wilson already the grinder (51 carries, 187 yards; Charbonnet is not in that rusher log), and SF's pass game is Kittle and Evans tied at 17 targets with CMC on a normal 40-carry/150-yard load plus Purdy's 12 designed rushes. No blowout flag can be set without a spread, so starter snaps are treated as safe in the base.
script.flip1: SEA jumps ahead and runs the clock: Wilson's carries rise, JSN's second-half routes stall (his most recent 76-yard game is the template), and SF trails so Purdy throws — Kittle and Evans targets rise while CMC's rush line dies.
script.flip2: Uncharted wind/rain or a slog in which SEA's charted sub-6.0 YPA travels: both receiving overs die and the game becomes CMC/Wilson carries with short checkdowns. A related flip is SF bracketing JSN while SEA's 21% blitz rate keeps Purdy in his worse no-blitz EPA state (0.31 vs 1.08 when blitzed).

injury_fallout: Source: official pre-game nflverse injury report plus weeks 2-4 carry/target sums. SEA RB Zach Charbonnet Out (knee) is already missing from the weeks 2-4 rusher list, so Wilson (51/187) is the established RB1, not a fresh next-man-up; J.Price (18/67) and George Holani (14/41 rush, 7 targets/52 rec, Questionable ribs) are the committee — Holani overs are a snap-limit risk until inactives. SEA LB Chazz Surratt Out (calf) is the TE/RB-receiving boost for SF: Kittle (17 tgt/232 yds) and CMC (14 tgt/102) gain; Kyle Juszczyk would have too, but he is Out (knee) and his 6 targets/55 yards/50 air have to be redistributed to CMC, Kittle, and Deebo's short role. SEA CB Julian Neal Out (hamstring) puts Evans (17 tgt, 260 air) and Samuel against an uncharted backup. Irvin Charles Questionable is not in the target log. SF DE Nick Bosa Out (knee), DT James Thompson Jr. Out, DE Mykel Williams Questionable: less real pressure, more time for JSN's 338 air yards; it does not automatically soften a run defense that has allowed 3.77 YPC. SF S Marques Sigle Out (ankle) and CB Upton Stout Questionable (shoulder) are the deep/perimeter hole for JSN and for Shaheed (147 air on only 69 yards). Final inactives about 90 minutes before kick are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Proxy only: SEA blitzes 21%, so SF mostly sees a non-blitz shell, and SEA's charted YPA is tight on every third (left 5.9 on 51 throws, middle 4.79 on 19, right 4.69 on 54). SF blitzes 31%; their YPA is softer, middle 6.38 on 16 throws, left 6.0 on 56, right 5.85 on 72.
matchup.pressure: SEA blitz 21%. SF EPA/dropback is 1.08 vs blitz and 0.31 vs no blitz, so Seattle's low blitz rate keeps Purdy in his worse state and caps SF explosives unless coverage busts. True pressure rate is not in the pack. SF blitz 31% but Bosa is out and Williams is questionable, so the blitz may not arrive; SEA EPA/dropback is 0.20 vs blitz and 0.19 vs none. Less pressure means fewer forced checkdowns and more time for JSN (338 air on 31 targets, 10.9 air/target).
matchup.bleeds: Charted SEA defense does not bleed: YPA 4.69-5.9, rush 3.73 YPC, only 5 passes of 20+ for 135 yards in 4 games, though they have allowed 9 runs of 10+. The prospective SEA bleed is injury-only — Surratt out on the hook/TE, Neal out outside. Charted SF defense bleeds the middle (6.38 YPA) and has allowed 6 passes of 20+ for 150 yards; Sigle out adds a deep hole and Bosa out adds time. SF run defense does not bleed (3.77 YPC, 3 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: The skill-core overlap is JSN, not an SF outside WR: 31 of 82 listed SEA targets (37.8%) with 338 air yards into a middle that already allows 6.38 YPA plus a missing safety and a missing edge. Second overlap is Kittle: tied for the SF target lead (17 of 70 listed targets, 24%) with 232 yards, and the LB who would sit on the hook is out. Evans has the same 17 targets and 260 air but no charted SEA side worse than 5.9 YPA, so his overlap is only Neal's unnamed backup. Deebo (10 targets, 33 air) does not attack a weak spot.

Kittle last4 rec yds 12, 80, 82, 70 — three straight clearances of 54.5 by 15+, but 232 yards on 146 air (13.6 YPT) is YAC-heavy and a regression tell; week-1 12 is the floor. JSN last4 122, 155, 128, 76 — the role is real (31 tgt/359 yds in weeks 2-4) but the sequence is declining through the 95.5 line. Evans 49, 54, 34, 76 vs 50.5, no trend, 164 yards on 260 air in weeks 2-4. CMC rush 68, 23, 75, 52 vs 49.5; weeks 2-4 were 150 yards on 40 carries (3.75 YPC), exactly SEA's 3.73 allowed. Purdy rush 29, 30, 35, 31, all over 23.5, on 12 carries/96 yards (8.0 YPC) — tight band but explosive-looking. Wilson rush 3, 92, 14, 81 vs 63.5, two busts and two explosions. Wilson rec 0, 0, 0, 39 — the only catch game is the most recent. Holani rec 0, 2, 48, 2, one long play. Deebo rec 48, 31, 0, 26; weeks 2-4 only 57 yards on 10 targets. Barner 13, 8, 69, 12, one spike.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and Kittle under 54.5 lost the over. SEA's charted pass defense (YPA 4.69-5.9, only 5 explosives of 20+ in four games) showed up even without Surratt: they bracketed the TE after three 70-yard games and lived with Evans, and 13.6 yards per target on only 146 air yards regressed into a 40-yard YAC day. SEA blitzed 21%, so Purdy stayed in the 0.31 EPA no-blitz state and the SF pass game never got the cheap explosives. The 54.5 coin-flip was the tell that the hot streak and the public injury report were already in the number. The same Monday, JSN at 95.5 would have lost because 76 was the start of the bracket, not a dip, and any uncharted wind killed a 10.9 air-yards-per-target role. That counter-case is why JSN is a pass and why Kittle is flagged rather than sized.
slip_story: One-story slip only, and it is a flag not a wager: SF throws in a competitive game, Kittle over 54.5 as the single leg. It does not stack with a game under, with CMC rush over (that needs a lead and a run script), or with JSN over (shootout, and that lean was dropped). Wilson/Holani are not sleeper adds — Charbonnet's absence is already in Wilson's 51 carries, and Holani is Questionable. No parlay, no TD, no receptions market, no second market on Kittle.
